title: 3.7.17 Lab: Build a New Array with Spread
description: Use spread to combine two arrays and to add loose values around a copied one, without changing any input. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create two arrays
steps.instructions: Create two variables, first and second, that each hold an array of at least two values.

steps.title: Combine them with spread
steps.instructions: Build a new array called combined that contains every value from both arrays using array spread.

steps.title: Add loose values around a copy
steps.instructions: Build another new array called framed that puts a loose value at the front and another at the back, with first spread in between.

steps.title: Log the results
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print both new arrays and one of the originals, to confirm the original did not change.

requirements.title: Spread used
requirements.description: Uses array spread, written as ... inside an array literal. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Spread is three dots in front of an array, written inside the square brackets of a new array.

requirements.title: Two spread arrays combined
requirements.description: Spreads two arrays into one new array literal. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Put both arrays, each with three dots in front, inside one new pair of square brackets.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: Arrays declared
requirements.description: Declares at least two arrays. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Declare two arrays in square brackets, each with at least two values.

requirements.title: both new arrays and an original are printed
requirements.description: At least three lines were printed: the combined array, the framed array and one original. Help: 3.7.14 (Reading: Spread Into a New Array)
requirements.hint: Print the combined array, the array with loose values around a spread, and one of the originals.

checks.expr: JSON.stringify(combined) === JSON.stringify([...first, ...second]) && framed.length === first.length + 2 && JSON.stringify(framed.slice(1, -1)) === JSON.stringify(first) && (J => combined.every(x => J.includes(String(x))) && framed.every(x => J.includes(String(x))))(output.join(' '))
checks.fail: combined should hold first then second, framed should be first with one loose value on each side, and your output should show both.
